creative-strategy.produces: Validated twelve-beat story arc (agent authors `creative/story.json`; missing beats fail). The story plan also names its VILLAIN (person or not a person: cancer, debt, a layoff, a lie, burnout, fear, the inner critic, a system) - see FU-U16 below.

script-lyrics.produces: Sung lyric script passing sung-copy rules (first-person, pronunciation, CTA). STOP RULE: at most 3 validator rounds (lyric_writer, check_lyric_sheet, words_fit); still failing -> stop, report the exact gate and ask the client ONE question; never grid-search, never exceed about 10 minutes, never edit a validator.

music.produces: Suno song master and timing map for the approved lyrics, on a reserved ledger attempt. This ONE command is the music stage on a clean install: it supplies the production transports itself (`scripts/core/song_transports.py` -- measurements decoded off each take's own audio, every paid take kept under `$RUN/music/takes/<variant>/take-NN/`, the one word-timing step, and the pace order), attaches the run's recorded four-pick card receipt, and hands the `script_words` gate the approved sheet's lyric lines. When the card's SONG APPROVAL answer is Yes it makes three labelled versions of the same sheet in parallel lanes (`generate_choices`), not one; orchestrated runs pass `--variant <variant_id>` or `--unit-id WW-00N` to make exactly ONE. The lower-level row below describes the one-song case only: `kie_dispatch.py dispatch --model <suno-model-id> --request "$RUN/music/req.json" --save-dir "$RUN/music" --ledger "$RUN/spend.sqlite3" --run-id "$RUN_ID" --logical-key suno --attempt-id a1 --cost 0` still works for a single hand-built job, but it supplies no transports, no receipt and no sheet words -- the `generate` row is the one to run.

continuity-bible.produces: Continuity-bible stage runner (one executable step, never a separate manual action): typed load of the agent-authored Character DNA + product DNA + style bible records (`continuity/qc-records.json` LIST shape with legacy dict-wrapper migration, `continuity/makers.json`), the `qc_gate` stage gate always against the DECLARED required evidence (`character_continuity.stage.REQUIRED_CHECKS`, never derived from the records that arrive), then the guarded `state_store` advance of the `continuity-bible` row and the seven downstream stages' rows reported back. `--action check` evaluates without advancing, `--action downstream` lists the seven downstream rows. The registry reconciler predicate is `character_continuity.stage.proven` (`register()` wires it into factory's `_RECONCILIERS`).

storyboard.produces: Speaker-visible shot list bound to lyric timing; fail-closed before storyboard approval (planner binding via `shot_planner.shot_planner.bind_plan`, import-only). Every villain carries its OWN shots tagged `villain` (or `villain_visibility` outside `none`); the shot's pain and rise tags ride the same shots (FU-U16).

image-keyframes.produces: Keyframe images for every planned shot, delivered only after `final_assembler`-independent QC records exist.

video-generation.produces: Per-shot video clips on reserved KIE attempts (model id from `video_router`). The lip-sync windows keep THIS row verbatim on the Agnes path too. MiniMax H3 (`minimax-h3/*`) refuses a hand-written prompt: build its request with `python3 scripts/core/prompt_templates/make_h3_request.py --spec <spec.json> --characters <chars.json> --first-frame-url <https url> --out "$RUN/generation/video-req/shot-NN.json" [--card-receipt ...] [--storyboard-plan ...] [--storyboard-review ...]`, which assembles through `prompt_templates.assemble_h3`, measures the model's own band (5,000-6,800 of a 7,000 cap) and attaches the matching `prompt_receipt`; never substitute another model to get a prompt through.

agnes-keyframes.produces: Agnes path only (`agnes.answer == "yes"`): the same keyframes from Agnes Image 2.5 Flash at 2K, no words in the picture (`onscreen_text.no_text_block()` in the prompt, bake or overlay per `onscreen_text.decide`), one spend_ledger row at cost 0 plus one quota row. Replaces the `image-keyframes` row; every other row is untouched.

agnes-video-segment.produces: Agnes path only: ONE fixed 10-second clip for segment `<segment>` (`segments = ceil(delivered / 10)`), run as a background job with at most 2 in flight, polling no faster than every 15 seconds, cost 0. `next` hands out one segment at a time and answers `waiting` (`agnes-video-running`, or `agnes-quota-next-day` until the next 00:00 UTC reset) while they run. Lip-sync windows never use this row: they keep `video-generation`.

qc-retakes.produces: Targeted retake plan naming only failed units, capped at 2 attempts per unit.

clips.produces: 3, 5 and 10 minute ads only: the 60-second and 90-second clips cut from the master on whole lines, hook placement kept (FFmpeg only, no spend). Prints `[]` for 60/90 s.

trailers.produces: Campaign runs only (`method.json` purpose `campaign`): `next` presents THIS row as the `clips` stage in front of `delivery`, and keeps presenting it until `$RUN/edit/clips` holds its cut files. Same `clip_cutdown.py` command as `clips`, read one way more: on a method campaign timeline `clip_cutdown.plan_clips` returns `trailer.plan_trailers` + `ad_clip.plan_ad_clips`, so the run gets two 60/90 s trailers (episode destination, "watch the full episode" end card) and two ad clips (offer destination), each recording its own source in/out and destination. Never a second command: one call makes both.

final-qc.produces: Approved final-QC verdict records on the rendered master (independent reviewer, UNAVAILABLE never passes).

delivery.produces: Delivery gate record over the final package (master + `delivery_variants` plan + receipts); board event follows via `cc_sync` (import-only).

argv: import json,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/core'); from platform_fit import platform_fit as pf; print(json.dumps(pf.check(pf.probe_file('<delivered-file>'), '<placement>'), indent=2, sort_keys=True))
platform-fit.produces: Paid and social runs only (`method.json` purpose `paid_ad` or `short_post`), and `next` carries this command on the `delivery` presentation so it runs before the delivery gate. One verdict for the delivered file against the researched spec row: `PASS`, `FLAG`, `UNDETERMINED` or `NOT_AVAILABLE`, with the row's source URL and read date. A row past its re-verify window answers `STALE_SPEC`, which is a FLAG naming the URL to re-read and never a PASS; nothing here is a second copy of the spec table (`platform_fit/platform-specs.json` is the one).
